## Libraries

We will use `tidyverse` suite for data manipulations and plotting, `patchwork` for putting several plots together, and `tikzDevice` for rendering to LaTeX. For mathematical symbol's rendering we'd also add package `amsmath` to the `tikzLatexPackages` options.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(tikzDevice)
options(tikzLatexPackages = c(options()$tikzLatexPackages, "\\usepackage{amsmath}\n"))


```

## Data import

We import both the empirical cumulative distribution functions for $N$ signals, as well as the analytical solutions.

```{r}

ecdf_tbl <- read_csv("ecdf_tbl.csv")
analytical_cdf_tbl <- read_csv("analytical_cdf_tbl.csv")

```

```{r}

selected_n <- 12
ecdf_tbl %>% 
  filter(harmonic_no == 1, N == selected_n) %>%
  filter(x < selected_n) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_step(aes(colour = signal_type)) +
  geom_line(data = analytical_cdf_tbl %>% filter(N == selected_n, x < selected_n),
            linetype = 'dashed', linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "r", y = "ecdf", colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
       title = str_interp("No. converters ${selected_n}, harmonic 1")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed"),
                     labels = c("simulations", "analytical")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") 

```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
tikz("envelopes.tex", standAlone = TRUE, height = 3.3, width = 3.4, pointsize = 8)
ggp
dev.off()

system("pdflatex envelopes.tex")
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
